title: Knowledge check: Understanding Express 4 and Express 5

questions.prompt: In Understanding Express 4 and Express 5, which statement best describes Major version differences?
options: Bound the request with a timeout, validate the returned shape and define an explicit failure policy. Retry only operations that are safe or protected by an idempotency mechanism.
Move all backend decisions into the browser and trust the submitted values.
Return the same success response for every request regardless of outcome.
Separate current Express 5 behavior from legacy Express 4 behavior. Confirm version-specific syntax against the migration guide and use regression tests instead of assuming compatibility.
questions.answer_key: Separate current Express 5 behavior from legacy Express 4 behavior. Confirm version-specific syntax against the migration guide and use regression tests instead of assuming compatibility.
questions.explanation: Separate current Express 5 behavior from legacy Express 4 behavior. Confirm version-specific syntax against the migration guide and use regression tests instead of assuming compatibility.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Understanding Express 4 and Express 5?
options: Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Treat Express 4-to-5 migration as a compatibility task: audit path patterns and API changes, rely on the documented promise-rejection behavior carefully, and run tests against all routes and middleware.
Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
questions.answer_key: Treat Express 4-to-5 migration as a compatibility task: audit path patterns and API changes, rely on the documented promise-rejection behavior carefully, and run tests against all routes and middleware.
questions.explanation: Treat Express 4-to-5 migration as a compatibility task: audit path patterns and API changes, rely on the documented promise-rejection behavior carefully, and run tests against all routes and middleware.

questions.prompt: A change related to Understanding Express 4 and Express 5 appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
questions.answer_key: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
questions.explanation: Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
